name: Dark Iron clan
summary: In Blackrock Mountain, the Dark Iron clan serves Ragnaros under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan. Driven from Ironforge in the War of the Three Hammers, they called the Firelord from beneath the earth and fell beneath his rule.

sections.title: The War of the Three Hammers
sections.body:
The War of the Three Hammers began when High King Modimus Anvilmar died. Three dwarven factions had shared Ironforge, but the Bronzebeards defeated both rivals in the civil war. They drove out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons.

Thaurissan swore vengeance and founded a settlement in the Redridge Mountains. His sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. Both assaults failed, and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on Thaurissan's stronghold. Desperate, he tried to free an apocalyptic being beneath the earth. His ritual broke through the world's core and released Ragnaros the Firelord.

sections.title: Shattered Lands and Bondage
sections.body:
Ragnaros's return shattered the peaks around him and formed Blackrock Mountain's blazing caldera. The Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes lie beside it. The cataclysm killed Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, and the surviving Dark Irons became the Firelord's servants.

Over the centuries, they built Shadowforge City in the mountain's lower chambers. Their artisans and sorcerers mastered stone golems, dark sorceries, and steam-driven siege engines. Under the watch of flamewakers and elemental overlords, they made weapons from the molten elements around them.

sections.title: Spreading Shadow
sections.body:
Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules the clan from his Imperial Seat in Blackrock Depths. He follows Ragnaros's orders and prepares for total war, while secretly plotting to overthrow the Firelord with the strength of all dwarven lands.

Dark Iron infiltrators and raiding parties strike in Loch Modan, Dun Morogh, the Badlands, and the Wetlands. Dark Iron forces and an ambassador are also inside Gnomeregan, though their precise role in its fall is unclear.

sections.title: The Stolen Princess
sections.body:
Princess Moira Bronzebeard, King Magni's daughter and sole heir, was taken by Dark Iron agents while traveling to Lakeshire. Magni believes she is an enchanted hostage held against her will in Blackrock Depths.

Rumors from Shadowforge City tell another tale. Moira has become Emperor Dagran Thaurissan's bride and embraced a place of power among the dwarves her father despises.

faq.q: Where is the Dark Iron capital located?
aliases: where do dark iron dwarves live
faq.answer: The Dark Iron capital, Shadowforge City, lies deep in the caverns of Blackrock Depths beneath Blackrock Mountain. Its great stone halls hold Senate chambers, barracks, and the emperor's Imperial Seat.

faq.q: Why do the Dark Iron dwarves have dark skin and glowing eyes?
aliases: why do dark iron look different
faq.answer: Dark Iron dwarves have ash-gray or dark skin and glowing red eyes. They live beneath Blackrock Mountain, but the precise cause of their appearance is unknown.
The emperor descends directly from the sorcerer-thane who led the Dark Irons into exile. He rules the clan from his Imperial Seat in Blackrock Depths.

faq.q: Why did the Dark Iron clan summon Ragnaros?
faq.answer: During the War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane faced defeat as the combined armies of Ironforge and Grim Batol marched on his city. Seeking a weapon to destroy his enemies, he performed an ancient ritual that shattered the mountains and enslaved his people.

The Thorium Brotherhood is a splinter faction of Dark Iron craftsmen who broke away from the clan. Based at Thorium Point in Searing Gorge, they trade with outsiders and seek their own fortunes, earning the lasting enmity of their former kin.

faq.q: Why are Dark Iron dwarves fighting in Gnomeregan?
aliases: why are dark irons with troggs
faq.answer: Dark Iron forces, including the Dark Iron Ambassador, are inside fallen Gnomeregan. Their presence suggests involvement with Mekgineer Thermaplugg, but their precise role in the disaster is unclear.

faq.q: Are the Dark Irons allied with the Blackrock orcs?
faq.answer: No. The Dark Irons once tolerated the Old Horde in the upper spire, but now fight a bitter turf war with the Blackrock orcs above. The Dark Irons hold the depths, while Rend Blackhand's orcs control the upper citadel.

faq.q: Why did the Dark Irons attack Grim Batol?
faq.answer: During the War of the Three Hammers, Sorceress Modgud led a Dark Iron army against the Wildhammer clan at Grim Batol. Khardros Wildhammer slew Modgud, but her foul sorceries cursed the fortress so deeply that the Wildhammers could never live there again.

angles.text: As a Bronzebeard, you know the Dark Irons as ancestral traitors and sorcerers. Their old grudges still threaten Ironforge's borders from Loch Modan to Dun Morogh.
As a gnome, you may wonder why a Dark Iron Ambassador is deep inside fallen Gnomeregan. The clan's role in its fall remains unclear.
As a blacksmith, you know Dark Iron smiths as masters of fiery metalwork. Their specialized anvils and forges deep in Blackrock Depths are needed to craft legendary armaments.
As an Alliance member, you face Dark Iron border raids and the threat posed by their capture of Ironforge's crown princess, Moira Bronzebeard.
As a Horde member, you clash with Dark Iron armies across the Badlands and the Burning Steppes. Both sides seek supremacy over the ruins around Blackrock Spire.
